newsitem.title: USA: Montana sues tobacco companies for health costs.
newsitem.headline: Montana sues tobacco companies for health costs.

text.p: Montana's attorney general sued major tobacco companies Monday to recover millions of dollars in state medical costs and to prevent the industry from marketing cigarettes to children.
The lawsuit, filed in state court by Attorney General Joe Mazurek on behalf of the state of Montana, was similar to those filed by other states against the tobacco industry.
"Recent events -- including the settlement talks with tobacco companies -- have convinced us that it's time for Montana to join this litigation," Mazurek said.
Montana is the 25th state to sue cigarette makers to recover the health care costs for treating smokers.

"By joining, we help move the case against Big Tobacco to critical mass -- that point where it becomes impossible for the tobacco companies to ignore the number of states demanding honesty and accountability," Mazurek said.
Montana's lawsuit alleged that the tobacco companies have conspired since the 1950s to suppress damaging information about the health risks of smoking.

The suit accused the companies of using false information to dispute the link between smoking and disease; conspiring to suppress information on the addictive nature of nicotine; and manipulating nicotine levels to keep smokers addicted.
The lawsuit also contended that the marketing campaigns of tobacco companies were targeted at children.
"This lawsuit is designed to halt the deception and make the tobacco companies take responsibility for their conduct," Mazurek said.

The lawsuit, filed in Lewis and Clark County District Court, seeks damages for health care costs borne by the state through its Medicaid programme, and for increased health insurance premiums that the state must pay for its employees as insurance costs rise to cover tobacco-related illnesses.
Montana's health department estimated that more than 200,000 Montanans use tobacco and that 1,500 state residents die each year from tobacco-related illnesses.
The state did not specify damages in its lawsuit, but estimated Medicaid costs related to tobacco use at more than $12 million a year.

Among the company's named in the lawsuit were Philip Morris Cos. Inc.; R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. and its parent RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.; American Tobacco Corp.; Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. and its parent B.A.T Industries Plc.; Liggett & Myers Inc.; Lorillard Tobacco Co., a unit of Loews Corp.; and United States Tobacco Co., a unit of UST Inc.
The suit also names the public relations firm of Hill & Knowlton Inc., as well as the Council for Tobacco Research-USA Inc. and the Tobacco Institute, industry lobby groups.
